calls.head: Power vs. Power
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending O'Reilly’s line (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Capitals’ first line is Tuch, Strome and Kyrou.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hutson has two goals as the Capitals get past the Predators
paras: Filip Forsberg opened the scoring for the Predators on the power play midway through the first, but Cole Hutson tied it 1-1 for Washington three and a half minutes later. Boone Jenner put the Capitals up 2-1 early in the second. Forsberg struck again just under five minutes later to tie it 2-2. Hutson scored his second of the night less than five minutes later to put the Caps back ahead 3-2. Ross Colton tied it up for Nashville early in the third, but that was the last goal the Predators would get. Alex Tuch put the Capitals ahead for good three and a half minutes later. The Predators’ Roman Josi finished with three assists.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Charlie Lindgren made 24 saves for the Capitals, and Juuse Saros stopped 25 of 29 at the other end. The Capitals moved to 8-4-0 and climbed to second in the Metropolitan, while the Predators fell to 4-4-5, slipping to sixth in the Central.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Capitals.
Jordan Kyrou has a point in six straight games.
The Capitals’ Jordan Kyrou played his 500th NHL game and had an assist.
